en: I am honored to serve at your pleasure.
I think you’ll find the service at The Baroness to be… exemplary.
I find perception and reality intersect far less than most would think.
May your time in New York be unforgettable.
After the ritual is complete, if you’d like tickets to South Pacific, don’t be afraid to ask.
(Alt: After the ritual is complete, if you’d like tickets to South Pacific, don’t be afraid to ask.)
At The Baroness, we always strive for perfection.
Today will be a day unlike any other, I assure you.
New York is a fascinating place, isn’t it? You never know who you’re going to meet.
It’s important to never overlook the help.
I’m afraid a doorman’s job is never done.
Alas, my duties at The Baroness consume me today.
Sadly, the guests at The Baroness demand my attention.
I think that today, I shall simply remain a humble doorman.
When you need me, I’ll be ready.
The Baroness will gladly open its doors to you, should you wish it.
Best of luck with the Patrons today.
I don’t feel the need to insert myself in the Patrons' little spat.
After the ritual, you should stop by our lounge. Francis makes a lovely Martini.
Good luck unburdening yourself from the Tome, Detective.
Thanks... wait. What do you know about the Tome?
The ritual is about to begin, perhaps we can discuss this later.
I wouldn’t dream of getting in front of you.
This could get a little rough. If you need help, let me know.
I appreciate your concerns for my safety, but they are unneeded. I’ll be fine.
I trust your father is doing well?
He is. I'll be sure to give him your well-wishes.
I'd like you to know, that while The Baroness has seen all manner of dignitaries and celebrities, your family stands a cut above the rest in terms of decorum.
You were terrible tippers. Polite though, and that counts for something.
How do you manage to treat people with respect when they look at you with contempt?
Your family has certainly found themselves in situations where the way you must conduct yourself is contrary to what you desire.
Are you comparing yourself to royalty?
Merely drawing parallels. I assure you, we do not compare.
Bebop, if we survive the ritual, please let me treat Miss Shelly to a spa day at The Baroness.
That’s rather kind of you. Thank you!
I wish I could offer more for her...
Well, that’s what the Patrons are for, mate.
So, uh... whatcha plan on doing once I pull 'em in?
That… kinda defeats the purpose of me pullin' ‘em in, right?
This isn’t gonna go well, is it?
Not the ideal pairing, no... but I’m sure we can make it work.
Lovely to see you again, Miss Calico.
You look like you haven't aged a day!
You need to tell me your secret.
Oh, that would spoil the fun.
You wouldn’t have it any other way.
So, are you just in New York for the ritual or do you have… "professional interests" in town?
I suppose it is a bit of a reunion of sorts.
If something happens to me, can you take care of Ava?
In the unlikely event of it being necessary, she will be treated like a queen at The Baroness.
You don't seem to be nervous about workin' with me.
I've found that to be a rarity.
Isn't it nice when life can surprise you?
Do your job, or I'm gonna tear through your little hotel.
I will do my job because I value excellence. But if we fail, you will not set one foot in The Baroness nor will you lay a finger on its guests lest your immortal life meet an ignoble end. Am I clear?
You strike me as a man who loves what he does for a livin'.
Hohoho, I definitely derive enjoyment from what I do.
Professor, a little birdie told me you have an anniversary coming up!
Indeed! I figure getting my body back is the best thing I could give her.
I just wanted to let you know that, when I could still eat food, one of my favorite places to go was Sunday brunch at The Baroness.
I will be sure to let Jacques know, it will make his day.
Most men would be terrified at what we’re about to face, yet you seem remarkably composed.
Not having a face helps hide the terror.
I appreciate that, I do, but please indulge me?
Paul wanted me to send his regards.
I daresay one of humanity's best.
Miss Graves. This is not my place, and it's most certainly out of character for me, but... you have so much potential.
We both know they didn't. If you ever want to talk, the proverbial door is open...
I'm excited to get a front-row seat to you throwing your life away for revenge.
It's not throwing it away if they die.
I'm sure your wife will see it the same way.
I forget myself, please accept my apology.
How are things at the Baroness?
They've been running smoothly since the Baxter Society's intervention.
It is. There are some sins that not even bottomless mimosas can make up for.
The Baroness still the most haunted hotel in America?
Just the tri-state area, I'm afraid. That ghastly business in Macomb pulled a lot of Midwest specters.
It's fine. I imagine today will put things back on track.
How lovely to be collaborating with the OSIC.
I assume there are no issues at The Baroness?
I assure you, if there were, I would be attending to them as we speak.
You know, I've worked with curators and mediums, but never a sandman.
We handle ourselves a little differently.
So I've heard. And I can't wait to have a front-row seat.
What naughty things have you been up to?
If you want the answer so bad, you can always try to pry it from my mind.
I'm not taking the bait, Haze.
You can't blame me for trying.
Where are you staying while you're in town, Sheriff?
The cheapest hotel in Hell's Kitchen that I could find.
That will never do! You should stay at The Baroness!
I'm a sheriff from the midwest; I couldn't afford that place even if I wanted to.
The stay would be complementary, please, I insist.
Bet you deal with all kinds of assholes at work.
I try not to judge the clientele. The intricacies of humanity are what make working in the service industry so fascinating.
You must have the patience of a saint.
In my experience, most people who've endured the kind of trauma you faced in Macomb crumble.
"In your experience"? Buddy, you have no idea what it was like.
Apologies, you're right. It was silly of me to imply otherwise.
Infernus, if you ever tire of Jezebel's please let me know. I think you would enjoy working in our lounge.
I respect your loyalty. Good luck today, Infernus.
It's funny how men like us can find comfort in the banality of people.
I think I'll be able to manage, but thank you for your concern.
You're the Savior of Spanish Harlem, everyone knows your name.
That makes me a little uncomfortable.
Then you're approaching your notoriety with appropriate gravitas. I look forward to seeing what life has in store for you.
Yes, Ivy, how may I help you?
Do you think it would be possible for Carlos to host a fundraiser at The Baroness?

That would depend on the nature of the fundraiser. The Baroness must be above politics. So, if this is to raise money for Mr. Arroyo's mayoral campagin, I cannot help you. If it is about his community efforts, a conversation can be had.
I don't suppose The Baroness is hiring?
Ivy, I would love nothing more than for you to be in The Baroness' employ, but I'm not sure it would make you happy.
In your world, you get to punch bad people. In mine, you have to smile at them and pretend they're right.
It's fascinating. But not for everyone.
I've heard there are fascinating mysteries afoot at The Baroness.
Oh, Kelvin. The things I have seen and heard are spectacular.
Perhaps I should arrange a stay?
I think that's a wonderful idea.
I'm so happy to see you, Kelvin!
To look at you is to look at the human condition: Proud, strong, capable of incredible things, but ultimately a slave to your own hubris. Truly, you are the total package.
Was that intended as a compliment?
It was neither barb nor balm. It's just the truth.
I don't know what you are.
Aren't you supposed to be a lover of the unknown?
This is a little different than an expedition.
This is true, you haven't led your fellows to their death yet, but there's still time.
Lash, this pains me, but I need a favor...
I would also like an 8 by 10.
You work at The Baroness, yes?
That hotel used to be magical, until its standards went to hell.
I will lodge your complaint with the management.
I hope you don’t expect a tip for helping me.
I wouldn’t dream of expecting anything from you, Lady Geist.
And how is Oathkeeper treating you these days?
You’re as charming as ever, Lady Geist.
You've really come up with ingenious ways for men to slaughter men.
The other Fairfax directors always host events for their teams at The Baroness, but you never do. Why is that?
It's the finest hotel in New York.
How are you doing, Miss Ha?
I try not to talk to the help.
So, what do you plan on doing to help? Holding open a door while I do all the work?
You could’ve at least changed when you got off of work.
Ah, but this one’s freshly pressed.
How do you like your stay at The Baroness?
How would you say we stack up to other accommodations?
Please fill out a comment card, I must know everything.
It is my honor and privilege.
Your loyalty to your charge is appropriate and inspiring.
Know that if you lose your life in service today, I will take appropriate care of Ambassador Nashala and transport her wherever she needs to go.
Thank you for banning Silver from brunch at The Baroness.
I don't take pleasure in it, but it was either remove her or remove the bottomless mimosas.
Well, our sofa and rug appreciate that you made the right choice.
Krill, feel free to cover Maurice's ears, but why are you living in a sewer as a common criminal, when a man with your intellect could get an honest job at a museum?
I imagine you would also enjoy having a duvet that isn't covered in black mold.
If life was perfect, it would be boring.
Would you two be interested in being kept on retainer? Some of our guests at the Baroness can have exotic requests that you both are more suited to catering to.
It's hard to picture Maurice and I running around in matching uniforms.
We may be too far apart, I'm afraid.
Very well. The hat can stay... but no vest.
You should host a storytelling event at The Baroness sometime.
The Baroness hosts a wide variety of guests. I’m sure most would be delighted to have you, and the ones that don’t will regret their decision later in life.
That’s very kind of you to say.
Yours is a rare gift. Only a fool wouldn’t delight in it.
So, how long have you worked at The Baroness?
Well, I tormented man for so long that serving them still retains its novel charm.
Don’t worry about it, the ritual is about to begin!
Well, I know that’s your job, ha! But what’s your name?
It’s not, but for my purposes in New York it helps me stay grounded, that I am here to serve and not to rule.
What you do on sabbatical is none of my business.
I don't fear you! It's just not worth risking the temper tantrum of an errant force of nature costing me the ritual.
I could think of some civilizations that would disagree.
Why would it? The pursuit of power is endless.
It's a good thing I'm not playing then.
How nice to see you sober.
You get kicked outta brunch one time, and everyone thinks they know you.
Can you put me up in a suite in the Baroness?
You know, the old me would've ripped your leg off for saying something like that... but the new me's just gonna rely on the vague threat of violence.
You gonna put me up in a suite or not?
Let's see how today goes, then we can talk.
You gonna mess with my head?
Heavens no, you have enough demons, you don't need my help.
Ah. I see we're both familiar with each other's work. How lovely.
Next time you visit New York, you should stay at The Baroness.
Oh, The Baroness definitely has my attention...
Wonderful! Any time you wish to enjoy our hospitality, please let me know. I'll make sure to attend to it personally.
Merely a simple servant, just like you.
After the ritual, you should stop by The Baroness. Our house tailor is top-notch, should any part of you… pop loose.
That place might be a little fancy for someone like me.
Oh, The Baroness does not discriminate, my friend. I assure you that you will be well taken care of.
I’m a shambling mass of dead bodies, what doesn’t trouble me?
You like working at the hotel?
Catering to rich people is rewarding?
Hey- Doorman, after the ritual, I just wanted to let you know that I'm gonna rob The Baroness blind, but you seem alright, so I'm just- I'm gonna let you go.
[Scoff followed by laughter that ends in a sigh]
Okay, well that was not the reaction I was expecting.
You look a little... prim and proper, buddy.
You only have one chance to make a first impression.
You got some ritzy people staying at The Baroness, don't ya?
We do cater to an upscale clientele, yes.
Alright, well, how 'bout this: You give me a list of the names, a housekeeping uniform, and a cloche; and you and I can be runnin' off to Tahiti by the end of the week.
I am neither betraying my guests nor going anywhere with you.
I need to be able to defend myself.
I'll do my best to slow down the mob.
Hurting them is fine, but vexing them is even better.
They will find fighting us more difficult than they expect.
Hard to shoot straight when your ears are ringing.
I'll influence the fight with a subtle hand.
Their aim will be less true.
If I need to intervene, so be it.
Allow me to deal with them.
I must be clever when placing these.
I will warp reality to my whim.
To those with real power, the rules of reality are mere suggestions!
I will build a path for my allies.
Such wonders I will show them.
To the clever mind, this will assure victory.
I will go where I desire.
I will bridge a gap between reality.
We will stride across time and space.
Allow me to be your guide.
Allow me to be of assistance.
It’s an honor to be of service.
I still have time to escape!
Time to get a little creative.
They won't get close to me.
I'll have the luggage cart ready.
I'll dismiss them with a wave of my hand.
Our enemies will be sent flying!
I'll launch them across the battlefield.
I have a way of dealing with unwanted guests.
If I may have a word.
I believe my assistance is needed.
I will warp reality to my whim.
The Baroness is ready to receive new guests.
Ready to tear their minds asunder.
Ready to take them to the Baroness.
Ready to pull them off the battlefield.
I will usher them to realms unimaginable.
Ready to show them what real power looks like!
Ready to warp time and space.
No one resists the call of the Baroness.
I look forward to checking in new guests.
The Baroness has rooms for everyone.
The Baroness will receive our foes with open arms.
I can't wait to see the comment cards our guests will fill!
I'll make sure the rooms are prepared.
They will never forget their stay at the Baroness.
The august halls of the Baroness await them.
They will die surrounded by the finest of luxury.
The Patrons won't mind if I put my thumb on the scale a little.
I’ll take you to your room.
The Baroness opens its arms for you.
I hope you enjoy your stay here.
Such secrets The Baroness can show you.
All you have to do is walk toward that door.
The Baroness is always looking for new guests.
I hope your time at The Baroness is Unforgettable.
Please, forgive the mess, The Baroness is mid-renovation.
You are, of course, welcome to stay at The Baroness for as long as you'd like. I do hope you enjoy your visit.
Right now, I'm sure your mind is reeling. Questioning your very eyes, if not your sanity.
The hallowed halls of The Baroness welcome all. We do not discriminate. Stay as long as you’d like.

Time slips away, as does your worry. Well, I suppose your worry is likely mounting as we speak, but eventually, it will give way to... inevitability. And from there, to the sweet blackness of the void.
Your friends are alone. Likely dying, while you sit here basking in the finest luxuries this plane can offer. You can try to save them, but why? You're already too late.
Why die on the streets of Manhattan, like a common criminal? Die here in The Baroness, like a celebrity, with creative demons and a substance abuse problem.

Personally, I’m impressed with your will to live. It’s futile, and pointless, but inspiring. Like watching a colony of ants, working to carry a strawberry, blissfully unaware of the gardener turning on the hose.
Thank you for giving your life at The Baroness Hotel. Gratuities are never expected, but always appreciated.
The Patrons have waited centuries to be summoned, they can wait a little longer. Stay. Enjoy the sauna and Egyptian cotton sheets. Let the troubles of the world melt away.
The Tome will pull you down with it, Abrams. It is inevitable.
The Tome is an impossible burden, detective. Why don’t you lay your head down and enjoy the amenities that The Baroness can offer?
Apollo... the ritual matters to this plane, not Ixia. Don't throw away your life to benefit some humans.
Apollo, how does it feel to be a part of a family so hated that children in Ixia sing a schoolyard rhyme about your mother being impaled on a tree?
Know this, Bebop: when Ms. Shelly dies, it will be because of your failure.
How much of your time is spent taking care of Ms. Shelly, Bebop? The double life you lead must be exhausting. Take some time for yourself, you deserve it.

Normally, I would take this time to make you confront your inner demons, but in order to do that, you’d have to be a person with some sort of actual passion and drive, but you’re not! You’re a caricature of outrage, a contrarian who thinks that hating something is the same thing as being interesting. So please leave, you’re dreadfully boring.
Look on the bright side, Calico. When your body rots, I’ll take care of your cat.

I see you, Calico. Your heart is cold, but it is not dead. There is a part of you that has not buried the past. It’s not too late to rethink your choices. Stay a while. The Baroness has a way of calming the tempest of the mind.
Lenny is lost, Celeste. But you need not suffer with him. It's safe here in The Baroness.
Your found family is doomed, Celeste. Even if you save Lenny's soul now, do you really think he won't just sell it again the next time it's convenient?
Reality twists and bends around you. How can this be? Has The Baroness turned on its loyal servant, or has a fledgling god lost his mind in the face of the Patrons?

Your heart beats faster as you find yourself in new territory. Slowly, but surely, realizing that here you are no predator, merely vermin scuttling down the hall. It won't be long before you find yourself feeling something that’s eluded you for centuries: Fear.
Professor, be honest with yourself: you’re never getting your body back.
Professor, a little birdie told me that your anniversary is coming up. How wonderful! I would love to extend The Baroness’ hospitality to you and your wife.
You wish to help the dead, Miss Graves? There are so many here that need you. Stay.

Miss Graves, you are so starving for a parental figure that you ran straight into the literal palm of a lich's hand. You know it's wrong, you know you can't control her. You know that you're going to die if you don't get help, and you're praying that your parents will notice before it's too late. They won't. But I see you. Stay at The Baroness, and let me be your teacher.
Talon, you couldn’t save your family and you can’t save yourself.

Wesley. You dedicated your life to protecting others, but in the end, you couldn’t protect your son. Or his wife. Or their children. How many moments of their lives did you miss because you were too busy? Because you were traveling for work, because your calling was important and your family would be there when you return. Yes, their lives were stolen, but it was you who robbed them of a father. Well done!
Keep calling yourself a Sandman instead of executioner. Maybe you’ll believe it.
The OSIC is lucky to have you, Haze. Your commitment to your work is an inspiration, but even you deserve some R&R. Why don’t you take a PTO day at The Baroness?
You failed to stop the Troubadour in Macomb, and you’ll fail again in New York.
I can only imagine the horrors you witnessed in Macomb. Rest, Holliday, and put aside your trauma for tomorrow.
You thought you put your past behind you, but it will be your undoing.
You ruined many lives, Infernus. Do you really think that saving Hank’s bar will make up for the harm you caused?
If you’re here with me, who is protecting the Arroyos from Mendoza?
Ivy, you’re a good person, and I have no desire to torment you here. Just know this: In five years, one of the Arroyos is going to die, and there is nothing you can do to stop it.
You pushed away Ettrick for his ambitions, yet remained a slave to your own.

You wrestle with so much guilt. The things you know you did and, even more horrifying, the things you forgot. But at The Baroness, you don’t need to worry about Ettrick or the expedition. Let me lighten the load.
That ward on your arm won’t hold forever, Geist. Oathkeeper is coming for you.
Lady Geist, I have the most wonderful room for two. I’m sure that you and Oathkeeper will be happy at The Baroness.
Oh look, a stevedore with delusions of grandeur.
Lash, Lash, Lash. You have been such a naughty boy lately. Whatever should I do with you?
Your creations are responsible for the deaths of millions, McGinnis. You’re a monster.

The pursuit of excellence is a marathon, not a sprint. And while you are miles ahead of your competition, you still have miles to go. So please, take this time to rejuvenate yourself and relax. Fairfax Industries will be there tomorrow. You can take some me-time today.
You’re a nobody, Mina. You don’t have a chance at becoming viscount.

Mina, Mina, Mina. Your future was stolen from you by an assassin’s bullet and replaced with the promise of eternal youth. We both know how well that’s turned out for you. You’re a child, just learning to play a game that others have spent hundreds of years perfecting. You are destined to fail.
Wyoming is a pipe dream, Mirage. The Djinn are doomed.
Wyoming can wait, Mirage. If your goal is to protect Nashala, there is no safer place in the world than The Baroness.
Maurice, Krill is just dead weight. Kill him.
Krill, Maurice would be better off if he never met you.

Maurice, Krill is dead weight. An albatross, whose petty schemes have driven you to hide in the muck, like a common criminal. But you’re not common, you’re exceptional. Free yourself of him and see this for yourself.

Krill, your brilliance shines in the dark, but it would be radiant in the sun. Why do you lower yourself to Maurice’s standards? Your blind loyalty to him has cost you opportunity after opportunity. Cast him aside. Accept who you are.
You’re not the hero of your story. You’re a footnote in mine.

Patience! You now find yourself the Alice to my Cheshire Cat. So please, indulge in your personal Lewis Carroll fantasy as long as you wish. Such wonderful sights and experiences await you here at The Baroness.
What will the Paradox council think when you fail in truly spectacular fashion?
I know what you’re thinking, Paradox. Sadly there are no tchotchkes for you to take as a souvenir from your time at The Baroness. Just the memory of an unforgettable experience.
Why couldn’t you have just died, like your family wanted? It would have saved us a lot of trouble.
Arin, your mother and father love you, and would be glad to see you come ho-... [Breaks into laughter] Sorry, I tried, but I couldn’t keep a straight face, you have no home.
Don't go, Rem, we have a very comfortable bed waiting for you.

Rem, if you continue to walk the streets of Manhattan, it is only a matter of time before you end up vivisected on a government table. But, if you stay here at The Baroness, I can provide safety and comfort.
Seven, your ambition got you killed once, why haven’t you learned your lesson?
I’d offer you advice, but I know you wouldn’t take it. Good luck on your pursuit, Seven. I hope, in the end, the price that you paid was worth it.
The Baxter Society will turn on you, Shiv. It’s only a matter of time.
You don’t belong in the Baxter Society, Shiv, you know this. But there will always be a place for you here at The Baroness.
There are no games to play with you, Silver, you already know your demons are going to win.

Oh, Lilah, where do I begin with someone as pathetic as you? The walls of your own making that ended friendships? The vices that you've become a slave to? Or perhaps this fantasy that one day killing Shiv and the Drifter will make up for all the lives that were lost because you just weren't good enough to stop them. I truly am spoiled for choice...
You will be bound to each other for eternity.
You were in love once, but that has given way to spite and jealousy. You don’t need a divorce, you need time together. Why don’t you stay in our honeymoon suite?
I know you're prepared to die here, Venator, which is good, because you shall.
You know, Rourke, one day you will actually believe the legend you sell to people, and on that day you will die screaming.
You weren’t made for great purpose, you were made on a whim, to satisfy some scientist’s hubris.
You’ve looked so hard for answers, Victor, yet they still elude you... It must be exhausting. Take a moment to rest. The mysteries of your past will be there tomorrow.
You can’t put a bullet through hate, Vindicta. Hathorne will win.
Vindicta, how many lives have you claimed? Do they weigh on you? If so, rest, and purge yourself of that nagging sense of guilt. If not, take a moment to revel in the fruits of your labor.
(Alt: Vindicta, how many lives have you claimed? Do they weigh on you? If so, rest, and purge yourself of that nagging sense of guilt. If not, take a moment to revel in the fruits of your labor.)
Humans don’t understand the problems of the Deep because they don’t care about the problems of the Deep.
I suppose The Baroness is much like the Cube. A warm refuge where you get to feel the glorious embrace of oblivion.
Oh, why bother taunting you, you’re going to die of liver failure anyway.

I’ve seen you eye The Baroness as you stumble through Manhattan. Wondering what life could be like if you were the sort of person worthy of its hospitality. Vyper, I’m here to tell you that you are worthy. Just stay. You belong here.
You’re not a man, you’re a war doll, fixing mommy and daddy’s failures.
What do you want, Warden? I can’t restore the childhood you were denied, but you can be happy here. All you have to do is choose to stay.
Your aspirations are about to come crashing down, Wraith. The house always wins.

You’re a gambling woman, right Wraith? I bet you don't have the will to stay here until I'm finished talking. You're probably scoffing at the idea right now: "why would I do that, there’s nothing to gain?” and yet you’re curious. Maybe the risk is worth the reward. Maybe there is a carrot at the end of the stick. Even as your life is slowly ebbing from your body, you wonder if this is a trick. Some sort of meta-commentary that is challenging you, and if you stay the course, riches await. They don't. Well, maybe they do, and this is part of the trick. Maybe I'm desperate to stall time because I need you to back out before you gain immeasurable power?.. Are you still alive? I can keep talking. You're fun.
The only way you’ll ever honor your brother is by falling on his sword.

Your brother died to save your life, Kaori, and what do you have to show for it? A life of exile in a country full of people that can't be bothered to learn your real name, and an organization that is a shadow of its former glory. Just give up Kaori. Sorry, I forgot it’s “Yamato” now.
It would appear I made a mess.
Little children playing at war pose no threat to me.
They have no idea the deep waters they now find themselves in.
The fool thought they could stop me.
I hope there's not blood on my uniform.
Look what you made me do.
I can't remember the last time I had to kill someone with my own hands.
I haven't forgot what you did.
You make for a lovely companion.
We complement each other nicely, don't we?
Old habits die hard, I'm afraid.
I've come this far, I might as well kill them all, I suppose.
So, it's to be a day of violence, I see.
Dispensing gratuitous violence is so much easier than I remembered!
In time, I will butcher you all!
I forgot how wonderful it can feel to be feared.
If you give up now, I'll throw in a free night stay at the Baroness.
You're running out of time to not be slaughtered like the lambs you are, just surrender!
I haven't slaughtered man like this for years, what a treat!
Mortals, your pointless lives are about to come to an end!
Don't you fools get it? I am the Patron you should worry about angering!
I'll crush them like the ants they are!
Now's the time to make them suffer!
What can bullets do to a god?!
The Baroness will call to them.
The Baroness calls from across the cosmos!
The magic of man will crumble.
Your magic will never harm me!
I will heal, and they will die.
I mustn't forget to upgrade my powers.
Time to pick up a trinket.
I should go by the Curiosity Shop.
I might want to buy an item.
I wonder what I can afford now.
I can afford something new at the shop.
It might be time to spend souls.
I should consider my next purchase carefully.
I have enough souls to buy something of real value.
I should see what the Shopkeeper has for me now.
I do believe that it's time to go shopping.
I can afford whatever the Shopkeeper passes off as luxury.
I shouldn't leave the souls lying around.
No sense in letting this go to waste.
I'm sure I'll find a way to spend this.
The objective is still destroyed, that's what matters.
The ritual is closer to completion!
Another part of the ritual complete.
I look forward to saying "hello" to some old friends.
Now, where did they run off to?
Oh, don't run and hide, we were having so much fun together!
There'll be more opportunities to kill them.
I look forward to meeting them again.
Come back when you find your courage, friend.
They thought they could actually stop me.
I won't be killed by the likes of them.
